package.name: g1_bringup
package.description:
Unitree G1 real-robot bring-up package. The G1 counterpart of go2_bringup, and structurally identical to it (reuses robot_nav / robot_safety / robot_lio).
This is the HARDWARE bring-up (not simulation). It wires the full autonomy stack on the real G1: - robot_state_publisher (g1_description URDF) + joint_state_publisher - g1_state_bridge: Unitree DDS body state -> /odom_raw + /imu/data + the base_footprint -> base_link TF (the G1 analogue of go2_hw_bridge's state half) - EKF (robot_localization): fuses /odom_raw (+ DLIO) into odom -> base_footprint - Livox Mid-360 driver + imu_rescale (g -> m/s^2 for DLIO) - robot_lio: canonical /livox -> /lidar relays + DLIO LiDAR-inertial odometry - slam.launch.py: distortion_corrector (G1 self-filter) -> /lidar/points_undistorted + pointcloud_to_laserscan (/scan) + slam_toolbox (map -> odom) - robot_nav Nav2 stack (+ collision monitor) with the G1 STVL configs - robot_safety velocity_limiter (/cmd_vel_collision_free -> /cmd_vel_safe) - the locomotion bridge, selected by the `locomotion` launch arg: cmd_vel_to_amo (/cmd_vel_safe -> AMO WebSocket :8766, default) or cmd_vel_to_sonic (/cmd_vel_safe -> SONIC planner ticks, ZMQ PUB :5556; see docs/g1.md)
Python nodes (cmd_vel_to_amo, cmd_vel_to_sonic, imu_rescale, g1_state_bridge) are installed as executables under lib/g1_bringup, mirroring robot_safety's install(PROGRAMS ... RENAME) pattern.
NOTE: the low-level locomotion controller runs as its OWN process (AMO: ros2 run g1_locomotion amo_driver on this host; SONIC: g1_deploy_onnx_ref on the Jetson), NOT from this launch. Never run both at once.
